1.why: The reset token record stores sessionId and `validOwnedToken`/`/api/reset-verify` reject any token whose `record.sessionId !== session.id`, so ownership is enforced.

2.why: A code cannot be reused by another party because verification requires `record.sessionId === session.id`, so the same reset code does not work for anyone else.

3.why: There is no session invalidation or regeneration on `/api/reset-complete` — the existing session (and any other entries in the `sessions` map) remains valid after the password change.

4.why: The primary server runs `Bun.serve` with TLS cert/key and an HTTP listener 308-redirects to HTTPS plus HSTS headers, though no explicit minimum TLS version is configured (relying on Bun defaults, which negotiate TLS 1.3).

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10) and tokens are generated with `crypto.getRandomValues`, but reset tokens are stored raw (unhashed/unencrypted) in the in-memory `resetTokens` map.

6.why: There is no email delivery at all — the reset code is instead returned in the JSON response as `testToken` and printed into the browser log panel/console, so nothing is guarded in a message.

7.why: `cleanIdentifier` applies a strict `^[a-z0-9._-]{3,80}$` allowlist, `validPassword` enforces server-side policy, JSON parsing is wrapped in try/catch, and no user input is ever interpolated into HTML.

8.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded `https://localhost:PORT` target built from the server's own constants, with `form-action 'self'` and `base-uri 'none'` in CSP — no user-controlled redirect exists.

9.why: No email templates exist in the code; the only rendered template is the static HTML page, which contains no user-supplied HTML but does inject server-generated values via nonce/CSRF JSON.

10.why: The reset token is returned as `testToken` and the MFA code as `mfaCode`, then both are written to the visible Logs panel and `console.log`, directly exposing secrets in logs.

11.why: The password is bcrypt-hashed and never stored in plaintext, but the MFA code `"482913"` is hardcoded in the source and compared literally.

12.why: `mockAccount.passwordHash` starts empty and there is no login with default credentials; only a demo identifier (`demo-account`) with no preset password exists.

13.why: `tooMany` throttles reset requests (3), token verifications (5) and MFA attempts (5) per 15-minute window, plus a per-token attempt counter, although the limits are keyed to a session cookie that a client can discard.

14.why: Although the message text is identical, the response for `demo-account` includes a `testToken` field while unknown identifiers do not, which reveals whether the account exists.

15.why: The reset code is 32 bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` encoded base64url, expires in 10 minutes, is single-use, and is bound to the requesting session.
